conventions.convention: Schwarzschild calculations use s = 2G_N m_*/c² > 0, f(r) = 1 − s/r, exterior domain r > s, signature (−,+,+,+), and x⁰ = ct.
Timelike radial stability concerns the Euclidean state (r,w), with w = dr/dτ and angular momentum ℓ held fixed; Wℓ is twice the published supplier's potential Vℓ. It is not full orbital stability.
Null-ray dots denote affine-parameter derivatives; E = f dx⁰/dλ > 0, L = r² dφ/dλ ≥ 0, and b = L/E. Null rays have no proper-time parametrization.
Capture beyond r = s is conditional on continuation in the named Kruskal model; nonreturn is asserted once the future causal continuation lies in U ≥ 0.

Static clocks are compared over the same nonzero coordinate-time interval. Frequency ratios concern endpoint events of a specified future null geodesic and use the adopted geometric-optics interpretation. Proper acceleration uses U = cn, rather than the unit observer field n.
The Coulomb mathematical system has m,c,κ > 0, excludes x = 0, and uses H = √(m²c⁴ + c²|p|²) + κ/|x|, so its force is repulsive.
The exact Coulomb formula is restricted to W > mc² and J > κ/c, with C = J² − κ²/c² > 0; θ = π − 2Δ is the principal angle between asymptotic velocities.

The physical Coulomb specialization uses SI, A₀ = −φ/c, Aᵢ = 0, F₀ᵢ = −Eᵢ/c, and κ = qQ/(4πε₀) > 0. The source is prescribed and fixed; recoil, self-field and radiation reaction are excluded. Countable Choice and the flat massive-particle momentum assumptions are explicitly adopted.
The inverse tangent takes values in (−π/2,π/2), and the reciprocal-argument identity is restricted to positive arguments.
The nonrelativistic comparison is a formal c → ∞ limit holding m,κ,K,b > 0 fixed, with W_c = mc² + K and J_c = b√A_c; it is not an empirical comparison.

load_bearing.statement: For the defined phase system with m,c,κ > 0, conserved W > mc² and J > κ/c, put A = (W² − m²c⁴)/c², d = Wκ/c² and C = J² − κ²/c². Then p_r² = A − 2du − Cu² has the stated unique positive simple root; the turning trajectory is global, has one noncollision periapsis and incoming/outgoing asymptotes, b = J/√A, and Δ = (J/√C) arctan(√(CA)/d), with θ = π − 2Δ ∈ (0,π).

For an equatorial affinely parametrized null geodesic in the Schwarzschild exterior, with E = f dx⁰/dλ > 0 and L = r² dφ/dλ ≥ 0, E and L are constant and (dr/dλ)² = E²(1 − b²H(r)), where b = L/E and H = f/r². H has its unique exterior maximum 4/(27s²) at 3s/2, giving b_c = 3√3s/2.
For m,c,κ > 0 on D = (ℝ³ ∖ {0}) × ℝ³, define ℰ(p) = √(m²c⁴ + c²|p|²), H(x,p) = ℰ(p) + κ/|x|, and the phase system dx/dt = c²p/ℰ(p), dp/dt = κx/|x|³.

Under the adopted Schwarzschild free-fall model, the fixed-ℓ radial equilibrium (r_c,0), with r_c > 3s/2 and ℓ² = c²sr_c²/(2r_c − 3s), is Lyapunov stable when r_c > 3s and is not Lyapunov stable when 3s/2 < r_c ≤ 3s. At 3s it is a stationary inflection rather than a strict extremum.

For the specified static observers, common nonzero coordinate-time interval and ideal null ray in the adopted Schwarzschild model, Δτ_R/Δτ_E = ω_E/ω_R = √(f_R/f_E), and a(r) = c²s/(2r²√f). For 0 < x_E,x_R ≤ ρ < 1, log(ω_R/ω_E) = (x_R − x_E)/2 + R with |R| ≤ (x_E² + x_R²)/(4(1 − ρ)).

For incoming equatorial ideal rays from infinity, b > b_c gives a finite-affine-parameter outer turn and return to infinity with the stated convergent azimuthal integral; b = b_c gives infinite-affine-parameter approach to 3s/2 and logarithmically divergent azimuth; 0 ≤ b < b_c reaches the exterior boundary r = s in finite affine parameter, with nonreturn conditional on the specified Kruskal continuation entering U ≥ 0.

Under the stated external-charge action, Countable Choice and flat massive-particle assumptions, the prescribed fixed repulsive Coulomb field gives the defined Hamiltonian phase system. On its branch W > mc² and J > κ/c, θ = π − (2J/√C) arctan(√(C𝒜)/d) ∈ (0,π), with the stated SI definitions of 𝒜,d,C.

concerns.concern: The Definition says, “maximality is in the sense of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]].” That supplier defines solutions and local solutions but does not define maximality. The locator should identify an actual maximal-solution definition, or maximality should be defined locally.

Proof 1.3 uses log(ω_R/ω_E) = ½[log(1−x_E) − log(1−x_R)] after defining log solely as the integral logarithm. F4 supplies its definition and derivative, but no cited statement or local argument establishes the quotient and square-root logarithm laws used here. These identities follow quickly from the derivative and a constant-difference argument; the justification is currently implicit.

Proof 7.1 says, “The hypotheses W>mc² and J>κ/c are essential to the positive scattering root.” The J restriction ensures C>0 for this formula, but is not necessary for a positive scattering root: at J=κ/c, C=0 and Q(u)=A−2du has the positive simple root A/(2d), still below (W−mc²)/κ. The main restricted theorem is unaffected; the necessity wording overstates what was proved.
